findings.claim: Main's ov-save-skill (ADR 0023) writes viking://user/jasper/resources/.map.md on Hermes's first save. fs/ls with show_all_hidden lists it, so after the merge the script's 'nothing else' check fails with 'unexpected top-level entry .map.md' unless the operator guesses --allow .map.md. The how-to only says to pass --allow for 'a name you created on purpose', which an operator who never made .map.md by hand will not read as covering it. Either accept .map.md by default in compare() (it is a known writer now, and the test already treats it as allowed) or name it in step 4 of the how-to.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan says.
The job copies only the four trees, blogs before blog-scraper, with --ignore-existing on both writes.
It rewrites blog-scraper's sidecars on their own pass and runs its checks in the order the plan asks, each with its own exit code.
The key cannot write the old bucket.
The script derives row ids the way OpenViking 0.4.17.1 does, and nothing in it writes the old bucket or the old schema.
Gates are green on my own stamp.
One non-blocking finding: the outcome check will trip on main's new `.map.md` after the merge.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: `stamp green: c6f675d0d32310f0135e8a52fedcc82c6a7835fe620d557a69a61bbf8a86b59d`.
pre_commit, cli_tests and rows r1 to r7 pass.
Image row id.
In 0.4.17.1, `collection_schemas.py:795` sets id = md5(`<account>:<seed_uri>`) on the `viking://` URI, before `vectordb_adapters/base.py:_encode_uri_field_value` stores it as `/user/...`.
For a level-2 row, `_seed_uri_for_id` returns the URI as is.
So md5('lab:viking:/' || stored uri) is the right id.
`update_uri_mapping` uses the same derivation.
The table has no `parent_uri` column, so rewriting `uri` is enough.
Regeneration set.
I ran `merged_directories` on the real listing (ov-objects.txt).
It gives argon, addyosmani, anthropic, deepmind, mistral, ollama, spotify and then blogs/: eight directories, which matches ADR 0022.
openai has no file on either side, only markers.
uber's files are all in blog-scraper, and the blogs side holds one empty directory and no sidecars, so the rewritten blog-scraper sidecars carry it.
Leaving both out is correct.
The only shared keys are markers and sidecars, so the hash check can never see a shared file.
The kept trees have no other dotfiles.
The 71 images are png, webp, jpg and gif, and all four extensions are in IMAGE_SUFFIXES.
Ollama sampling risk.
`semantic_dag._dispatch_dir` sorts the direct entries by name and runs `deterministic_sample(…, 32)`.
I simulated it on the merged listing.
For ollama, 63 entries reduce to 32, and `windows-preview.md` (one of the two blogs-side children) is in the sample.
Overviews resolve child links to real URIs, which carry the child name.
The check needs any one name per half, so it can pass.
If the model leaves it out, the check fails loudly instead of passing wrongly.
Every other merged directory samples all of its blogs-side children.
Key.
Statement 1 grants only GetBucketLocation, GetObject and ListBucket on `openviking` and `openviking/*`.
Statement 2 grants `local.seaweedfs_write_actions` on `openviking-v2` only.
There is no other policy for the user, and it is not in `local.buckets`.
The `openviking` key already showed this ARN shape keeps the two buckets apart.
r4's test parses the statements and bounds the old bucket's actions to the three reads.
No writes to the old side.
In the job, `$old` is only ever a source (copy, check, lsf).
Every write goes to `$new` or a local tmp.
In the script, `openviking.ov_context` appears only in SELECTs and in the FROM of the INSERT…SELECT into `openviking_v2`.
Eval rows r1 to r7.
Each test asserts its fails_when.
r1 checks the refused tree (exit 5, nothing copied), the top-level set and the --ignore-existing flags.
r2 would catch a scraper copy that includes sidecars, a missing rewrite or an overwrite.
r3 seeds regenerated shared sidecars and expects exit 0, plus one case for each of codes 2, 3, 6 and 7, all distinct.
r5 checks the order, the rows-after-reindex step and the new id with no old id.
r6 covers each defect kind.
r7 checks the parent path and the source list.
r8 (judgment).
The how-to produces every piece of evidence the row names.
Step 3 gives the job's exit code.

Step 4's script prints each re-index result with failed and unsupported counts, then checks counts, the union and the since-cutover notes, the merged overviews, the 52 image rows plus a find by name, 10 title finds per tree, and the top-level "nothing else".
Step 5 diffs the old bucket against the cutover baseline.
The `--format pst` baseline parses with `read_listing`.
The task polling and the `failed_records` field match `reindex_executor.py` and `tasks.py`.
The check covers only `user/jasper/resources/`, which is the one place the carry-over writes.
Caveat: see f1.
Consistency: reference/openviking.md (exit codes, key scope), the seaweedfs and openviking-service components, the storage.tf comments, the OpenViking README and ADR 0022 agree with the code.
f1: `.map.md` from ADR 0023 is a top-level name the check rejects by default.
This is a plain fix: a default allow, or one line in the how-to.
ADR 0022's Context says the two blog trees "hold the same eight sources".
blog-scraper also holds nvidia, deepseek, `_lockprobe` and some loose posts.
Loose wording, worth a touch if you are in the file anyway.
`_lockprobe/Example_Domain` (a probe artifact) carries into `blogs/`.
The plan says to copy whole trees, so this is the operator's call.
`reindex()` treats a `cancelling` task status as finished and failed.
That is fine.
